newsitem.title: UK: IGC ups 1996 wheat output forecast to 573 mln T.
newsitem.headline: IGC ups 1996 wheat output forecast to 573 mln T.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) on Thursday increased its 1996 output estimate for wheat to 573 million tonnes from a previous 571 million.
In its latest monthly report, the IGC said it raised the estimate for the European Union (EU) to 98.1 million tonnes from last month's 96.1 million as more information was now available.

"Yields were higher than expected in the EU, China and Australia," said the IGC. The production forecast for China was increased by one million tonnes to 107 million while Australia was seen harvesting 20.2 million tonnes this year compared to last month's estimate of 19.0 million due to more favourable weather.
Kazakhstan's crop estimate was lowered by 1.5 million tonnes to 9.5 million while as harvesting was delayed due to lack of machinery.

The forecast for the Ukraine was down by 500,000 tonnes to 14.0 million. "The state procurement system finds it difficult to achieve targets as farmers are eager to sell grain at higher prices to private buyers," said the IGC on the Ukraine.

Russia's estimate was unchanged at 34 million tonnes, up by 4.0 million tonnes from 1995 when drought ravaged the crop while Brazil's estimate was raised by half a million tonnes to 3.0 million tonnes, double that of 1995.

The IGC kept its estimate for wheat stocks at the end of the 1996/97 season at a flat 104 million tonnes, and while this level of stocks was 11 million tonnes more than last season, it was still the second lowest since 1980.
"End-year carryovers in each of the five major wheat exporting countries will probably increase, the biggest rises being in the EC and the U.S.," the IGC said.
Bill De Maria, assistant executive director of the IGC, said despite the oversupply of crops, the world market was operating in a narrow demand/supply band without a large cushion of stocks.
